newsitem.title: ITALY: Telecom Italia strikes Seat sale deal.
newsitem.headline: Telecom Italia strikes Seat sale deal.

text.p: Italian telecom group Telecom Italia has reached a deal with Banca Commerciale Italiana to take an indirect stake in publishing firm Seat, the firms said in a joint statement.

A group led by bank BCI, which includes publishers De Agostini, announced last month it would pay 1.58 trillion lire ($890.7 million) for 61.7 percent of Seat ordinary shares, currently owned by the Italian Treasury.

Telecom, anxious to have a stake in the firm which publishes Italy's yellow-pages phone directory, has signed a deal with BCI to buy 20 percent of the holding company which has been especially created to purchase the Seat stock.
The holding is called Otto Spa, and is backed by eight investors, including BCI, Telecom, and Citicorp.
Otto will have share capital of one trillion lire, with Telecom Italia providing up to 200 billion lire of this.
Telecom, which is due to be privatised in October, will also provide other, undefined guarantees, to allow the Seat acquisition to go ahead.
"The participation of Telecom Italia in this operation has the characteristics of a financial investment in a sector connected to the telecommunications sector," the statement said.

The Treasury spun Seat away from state telecoms holding Stet earlier this year, saying the profitable publishing group needed to be sold off before the privatisation of the telecoms sector could go ahead.
Stet was last month merged into its operating division, Telecom Italia.

Stet and Telecom managers openly questioned government plans to sell its stake in Seat and with Monday's deal, the telecom giant has succeeded in retaining an important say in the publishing division. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501 ($ = 1773 Italian Lire)
